name: Display refresh rate and HDR
plain: Reads the screen refresh rate and HDR support with no prompt.
meaning: 60, 90, 120 or 144 Hz plus HDR format list separates device tiers and models. Used for animation pacing.

ios.api_surface: 60 or 120 Hz (ProMotion); ProMotion on Pro models since 2021

limits.headline: Can see your screen refresh rate and whether it shows HDR, with no prompt
limits.user_action: Nothing. Games and video apps check when they start
can: See the refresh rate, such as 60, 90, 120 or 144 Hz
See which refresh rate options your screen supports on Android
See if the screen supports HDR on Android
See if an iPhone has a 120 Hz ProMotion screen
cannot: Change the screen's hardware refresh options
Force a rate your screen does not support
Tell who you are from the screen alone
limits.differs: Android lists many refresh modes. iPhone shows 60 or 120 Hz, with ProMotion on Pro models since 2021.

story.what_it_is: An app can see how fast your screen redraws and whether it supports HDR.

marketing.name: Frame rate on Android
marketing.pitch: Developer guide: let your app choose a frame rate that fits the display for smooth motion and better battery life.

story.for_you: You see smoother scrolling and games on a fast screen. The app also learns whether your phone has a 60, 90, 120 or 144 Hz display, which shows the phone tier.
story.for_makers: Makers match animation speed to the screen and decide whether to offer HDR video. The mix of rate and HDR formats helps separate phone models for fingerprinting.

use_cases.example: A racing game offers a 120 frames per second mode only on phones that can show it.
A streaming app plays HDR movies only if your screen supports the format.
A drawing app matches pen lag to the screen speed so strokes feel instant.
A feed app speeds up scrolling animations on a 120 Hz display.
An AR app picks a target frame rate that matches the camera and screen.
An ad firm uses refresh rate and HDR formats to tell similar phones apart.

story.android_note: Reads the display modes and HDR list with no prompt.
story.ios_note: Reads the maximum frame rate and HDR support with no prompt.
